# Helping your midwife find you
### A friendly guide for Riverside home birth families

When you’re having a baby at home, the last thing you need is a midwife circling the block, waving at the wrong house—or being welcomed by a very enthusiastic dog while carrying a cylinder of gas and air.

We want getting to you to be as calm and quick as possible. A little preparation can make a big difference, especially at night. Please don’t worry if everything isn’t perfect: we’re coming to support you, not inspect your hallway.

## When to call

Riverside home birth cover starts from **37 weeks of pregnancy**. If labour starts before 37 weeks, contact the maternity service you’ve been advised to use. You’ll need to go to hospital for care.

From 37 weeks, when you think labour has started, **phone the Riverside birth line**. Please don’t call your midwife’s personal mobile: the birth line goes to the midwife who is on call and can arrange the right help.

Keep the number somewhere easy to find, such as in your phone and on the fridge. If you’re unsure what to do, call the birth line and speak to the midwife. They’ll talk it through with you.

## Help us find the right door

Sat navs are helpful, but they don’t always understand Liverpool. A house with no number and a name like “Rosemary Cottage” once sent a midwife to a chippy. Tempting, perhaps, but not the birth address.

When you call, tell us:

- Your full address, including the postcode.
- The house or building number and name, if there is one.
- Any details that could be confusing: several buildings with the same number, a shared entrance, a block of flats, or a hard-to-find lane.
- The best entrance to use, and how to get there from the main road.
- Your flat number and which floor it’s on. In some blocks, flat 14 is nowhere near flat 13.

If the address is tricky to find, you can send a location pin on WhatsApp to the **Riverside birth line phone**, or share a what3words location. Please check which entrance the pin points to and add any useful directions. A pin is a helpful extra, but it’s not a replacement for your full address.

If you can, have someone meet us outside or wave from a window. One dad used a tea towel to guide a midwife to the right building. It worked beautifully—and is easier to spot than a midwife guessing between identical blocks.

Balloons on the gate or a clear sign can help too. Just make sure anything you put outside is safe and won’t block the path.

## Make the arrival easy

At night, please switch on the porch or outside light. In a dark winter street, every front door can look the same.

Keep the path, hallway and stairs as clear as you can. Move shoes, washing baskets, toys and anything else that could trip someone. **No Lego on the stairs, please: it is a hazard even when there isn’t a baby on the way.**

Two midwives usually come to a home birth, often in separate cars. If possible, leave space for two cars. We may also be carrying a lot of equipment, including the big midwifery bag, gas and air equipment, and sometimes items for a birthing pool. A clear parking spot and easy route to the door are a very welcome start.

Some streets in Anfield and Kensington have permit parking. Please check what applies on your street. If you need a visitor permit, ask your council about the arrangements and have it ready as advised. If your council’s rules allow, you may be able to leave a permit on the dashboard. A parking ticket is not the souvenir we’re hoping to take home.

## Pets and little helpers

We love meeting family pets, but labour can be busy and a dog’s enthusiastic welcome can make it hard to carry equipment safely. Please settle pets in another room or with someone who can look after them while we’re there—especially when the midwife arrives and during pushing.

If your pet is likely to bark, jump up, or get excited by visitors, let us know when you call. We can make a plan together. Pippin the staffie may have been full of love, but a midwife carrying gas and air needs both feet on the floor.

## A warm welcome, not a perfect house

You don’t need to tidy the whole house or put the kettle on. We’re coming to care for you and your baby, like a trusted friend who also happens to bring a very full bag. Tell us what you need, ask questions, and let us know about anything that would help you feel comfortable.

A clear entrance, a working light and a good address matter far more than a spotless living room.

## Fridge checklist

**Before 37 weeks**
- [ ] I know that Riverside home birth cover starts at 37 weeks.
- [ ] I know which maternity service to contact if labour starts before 37 weeks.

**From 37 weeks**
- [ ] The Riverside birth line number is saved in my phone and easy to find.
- [ ] I’ll call the birth line when labour starts—not my midwife’s personal mobile.
- [ ] I know my full address, postcode, house or building name, and flat number.
- [ ] I’ve written down any tricky directions or entrance details.
- [ ] If useful, I can share a location pin or what3words location with the birth line phone.
- [ ] The porch light works, and someone can guide the midwives if needed.
- [ ] The path, hallway and stairs are clear.
- [ ] We’ve thought about parking for two cars and any permit arrangements.
- [ ] We have a plan to keep pets safely in another room.

We look forward to coming to you. And if you see a midwife looking uncertain outside, a wave from the window is always welcome.
